notes: The raspberry-pi-4 catalogue card (checked with lookup_part) has no individual GPIO pin ports. Its only header port is GPIO_HEADER. So the four wires that go to the Pi all use pi1:GPIO_HEADER, and the pin each one uses is given here instead.
Pin per wire: wire3 goes to GPIO14 (left button), wire4 to GPIO15 (right button), wire5 to GPIO4 (LED anode strip) and wire6 to GND (physical pin 9, next to GPIO4). The wire labels also say this.
The board is raspberry-pi-4 because the image shows the 2x20 (40-pin) header of a full Raspberry Pi and the manual's parts list says '1 x Raspberry Pi'.

Breadboard naming follows the catalogue: rows a-e are bank 't' and rows f-j are bank 'b'. The blue rail at the bottom is 'bn'. Rail hole numbers are counted in groups of 5 from the left: the left button's black wire is at bn.1, the resistor at bn.10, the GND wire at bn.19 and the right button's black wire at bn.25.

The left button is in columns 1 and 3 and the right button in columns 28 and 30. Per the text, each button's legs are in rows h and j, so the two legs in one column are the same side. The wires are in row f of those columns.

The LED's long leg (anode) is in column 16 and its short leg (cathode) in column 15, both on row e as in the image. The resistor is in column 15, row a, in the cathode strip, and its other leg goes to the blue GND rail. GPIO4 goes to column 16, row a, the anode strip.
For the male-to-female jumpers, port 'a' is the male pin end into the breadboard and port 'b' is the female socket end on the Pi header. The two black pin-to-pin wires are plain jumper-wire types.
